# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/golden/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tools/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(committed, `memory/note/` — the user's files: read freely, write only via
`memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/golden/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/golden` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);

data.content:
# gh-2185 seam map — runtime-state JSON writers + ExecutionEnv IO

All paths repo-relative. All stores share ONE pattern: private ctor holding `ExecutionEnv? _env` (null = inMemory), `static const fileName`, `load(env)` reading `env.readTextFile('${env.cwd}/$fileName').valueOrNull`, write via `env.writeFile('${env.cwd}/$fileName', jsonEncode({...}))`, both wrapped in `try/on Object {}` (best-effort, corrupt/missing → defaults). No store writes anywhere else.

## 1. ChatPinStore + ChatReadCursorStore — `flutter_app/lib/ui/chats/chat_list_stores.dart`
Import: `package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (:4). ChatPinStore class :10, `fileName = 'chat_list_pins.json'` :19, `load` :30–55 (read at :36), `setPinned` :57–64, `_save` :66–83 (write at :71).
**ChatReadCursorStore** class :90, `inMemory` :93–99, `fileName = 'chat_read_cursors.json'` :101, `load` :113–141 (read `'${env.cwd}/$fileName'` :119), `markRead` :145–150, `_save` :152–163 (write :157). Envelope `{'version':1,'accounts':{account:{id:cursor}}}`.
**Construction sites (only one production caller):** `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/wide_layout_shell.dart` `_ensureChatStores()` :374–391 — `ChatPinStore.load(env, accountId: key)` :384, `ChatReadCursorStore.load(env, accountId: key)` :387; `env = widget.manager.active?.service.env` :381; `key = networkSessions.accountLogin ?? 'local'` :375–376. Triggered from `initState` :592, `_onManagerChanged` :397, `_onNetworkSessionsChanged` :365. Fallbacks: `ChatListController` ctor defaults `ChatPinStore.inMemory(accountId:'local')` / `ChatReadCursorStore.inMemory(accountId:'local')` (`flutter_app/lib/ui/chats/chat_list_controller.dart` :26–37); `WideLayoutShell.initState` :575–588 passes injected `widget.chatPinStore`/`chatReadCursorStore` or inMemory, then `_ensureChatStores()` swaps real stores in via `_chatController.replaceStores` :390.

## 2. LauncherLayoutStore — `flutter_app/lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart`
`fileName = 'launcher_layout.json'` :76, `_version = 2` (v1 migrates) :80. `load(env)` :125–129 → `reload()` :136–143 → `_read(env)` :392–405 (read :394). `_mutated()` :359–363 → `_save()` :365–388 (write :370). Envelope `{version, order, folders:[{id,name,tiles}], grid:{columns}, tileSizes:{id:"WxH"}}`.

/// The `memory:` section of `~/.fah/config.yaml`: where the long-term
/// memory stores live. Defaults (no section) keep the historical layout —
/// `<projectRoot>/.fah/memory` and `$HOME/.fah/memory`. Setting
/// [projectPath] inside the repository (e.g. `./memory`) makes the
/// project memory committable: anyone cloning the repo gets its memory.
library;

import 'exceptions.dart';

/// Parsed `memory:` section. Both fields optional; null = default path.
final class MemoryConfig {
  const MemoryConfig({this.projectPath, this.userPath});

  /// Parses the section strictly: a non-map node, unknown keys, and
  /// non-string values throw [ConfigException] (a typo must surface, not
  /// silently write memory somewhere unexpected).
  factory MemoryConfig.fromYaml(Object? node) {
    if (node is! Map) {
      throw const ConfigException(
        'memory: section must be a map (projectPath/userPath)',
      );
    }
    String? projectPath;
    String? userPath;
    for (final entry in node.entries) {
      final key = '${entry.key}';
      final value = entry.value;
      if (value is! String) {
        throw ConfigException('memory.$key must be a string path');
      }
      switch (key) {
        case 'projectPath':
          projectPath = value;
        case 'userPath':
          userPath = value;
        default:
          throw ConfigException(
            'memory: unknown key "$key" (known: projectPath, userPath)',
          );
      }
    }
    return MemoryConfig(projectPath: projectPath, userPath: userPath);
  }

  /// Project-scope storage path. Absolute used as-is; relative resolves
  /// against the project root.
  final String? projectPath;

  /// User-scope storage path. A leading `~/` expands against the user
  /// home; absolute used as-is; relative resolves against the user root.
  final String? userPath;

  /// Resolves [projectPath] against [projectRoot] (null → the default
  /// `<projectRoot>/.fah/memory`).
  String resolveProjectPath(String projectRoot) {
    final path = projectPath;
    if (path == null || path.isEmpty) return '$projectRoot/.fah/memory';
    if (path.startsWith('/')) return path;
    final stripped = path.startsWith('./') ? path.substring(2) : path;
    return '$projectRoot/$stripped';
  }

  /// Resolves [userPath] against [userRoot] (null → the default
  /// `<userRoot>/.fah/memory`; `~/x` → `<userRoot>/x`).
  String resolveUserPath(String userRoot) {
    final path = userPath;
    if (path == null || path.isEmpty) return '$userRoot/.fah/memory';
    if (path.startsWith('~/')) return '$userRoot/${path.substring(2)}';
    if (path.startsWith('/')) return path;
    final stripped = path.startsWith('./') ? path.substring(2) : path;
    return '$userRoot/$stripped';
  }
}

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they are reported, which is
  why it is mandatory.
- **Live re-read surfaces**: in a running REPL, `/tools reload` and
  `/mcp reload` re-read their sections immediately and print the parse
  error instead of applying it — use them as the live check when a REPL
  exists.
- Runtime objects keep the last good config when a reload fails (the failed
  section never half-applies), so a loud reload error means "nothing changed".

## Provider & keys

<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->

User file, top-level keys:

```yaml
provider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Saved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique
    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter
    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1
    modelId: llama3            # non-empty
    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value
    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)
```

Applies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>
[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.
Keys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,
then endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name
store entries. `/key set|delete` manages the store and has NO config.yaml
equivalent — that is deliberate.

## Models & roles

<!-- parity: /model /models /model-edit -->

User file. The active model is the `model:` top-level key (above). Optional
sections:

```yaml
roles:                         # intent → ordered fallback chain
  default:
    - openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    - provider: openai         # or a map entry:
      model: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY   # optional; also baseUrl, contextWindow, maxTokens
      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000  #   (slow local model recipe, see below)
      thinkingLevel: high       # optional: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max
                                # (xhigh/max fold to high) — reasoning request
  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # roles: default, smol, slow, plan, subagent, memory
modelOverrides:                # scope chains to path prefixes
  - path: ~/work/acme
    roles:
      plan: [anthropic/claude-opus-4-5]
retry:                         # chain fallback policy
  retriesPerEntry: 2           # + baseDelayMs, maxBackoffMs, maxWaitMs, keyBackoffMs
providerTimeouts:              # GLOBAL fallback: only these two keys
  connectTimeoutMs: 180000
  streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000
agent:                         # strict: contextWindowCap (issue #273) +
                               # foreground-call budget keys (issue #1786)
  contextWindowCap: 262144     # owner context cap; min 16384 = the compaction reserve
  foregroundCallBudgetSeconds: 600  # foreground tool-call budget B in seconds;
                                    # int > 0, default 600 (10 min)
  foregroundCallAutoConvert: offer  # rung-1 behavior at B/2: offer (default, ask)
                                    # or auto (convert to background unattended)
images:                        # session image registry (strict): send-once
  registry: true               # kill switch — false = byte-for-byte legacy
  maxPerRequest: 20            # per-request unique-image cap (default 20)
models:                        # media slots + named custom models
  slots:
    vision:
      providerKind: openai-completions
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      modelId: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY
    imageGeneration:           # aiin media example (any OpenAI-wire
      providerKind: openai-completions   # provider works the same way:
      baseUrl: https://api.aiin.by/v1    # minimax, zai, a saved custom…)
      modelId: google/gemini-3.1-flash-image
      apiKeyName: AIIN_API_KEY   # sk-aiin-… key name (/key set AIIN_API_KEY)
    audioTts:
      useMainConnection: true    # explicit per-slot opt-in: this slot is
                                 # served by the main connection itself
    musicGeneration:
      unsupported: true          # explicit per-slot opt-OUT (issue #2085):
                                 # the capability is removed — media tools
                                 # refuse the slot, pickers stop suggesting it
  custom:
    fast:
      provider: openai
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      model: gpt-4o-mini
      contextWindow: 128000    # + maxTokens, input
```

Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554): `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`
are valid on `roles:` chain entries, `customProviders:` entries, and
`models.custom:` entries. Per field, the first level that declares a value
wins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >
global `providerTimeouts:` > built-in default** (connect 180 s, idle 300 s;
hard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.
Slow-local-model recipe: on the role entry that pins the local endpoint set
only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` ≈ 2× the model's worst silent prefill stretch —
the cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,
and the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Media slot names (exact): `imageGeneration`, `audioTts`, `musicGeneration`,
`videoGeneration`, `vision`, `transcription`. A slot without an override is
UNCONFIGURED — media calls fail with an actionable "configure the slot"
error; the main connection serves a slot only through the explicit
`useMainConnection: true` opt-in, and `unsupported: true` removes the
capability entirely (media tools refuse the slot, the pickers drop it from
capability hints).

The `images:` section has no settings-hub editor — the registry is runtime
state, not a persisted setting: `/images` (CLI) and the app's image-drop
chip/panel render the shared window/cap/drop projection, and the drop
notice model is latched (one notice per meaningful change, issue #1889;
see `docs/images.md`). The three keys above are the whole config surface,
applied at next boot.

CLI equivalents: `/model <id>` switches the active model (a
`models.custom.<name>` switches provider+endpoint+model in one step);
`/models config` displays this section, `/models set <slot> <model>
[baseUrl]` and `/models remove <slot>` edit `models.slots`;
`/model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]` overrides token limits for the
session (persist per chain via `roles:` entries instead) — bare in the TUI
it aliases into `/settings` → Model capabilities, the one surface that pins
`models.overrides` (issue #1515). Role edits apply at next boot; `/model`
applies live.

## Provider queue

Project or user file section; the `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var carries
the same JSON list and WINS over both files (issue #418). The ordered
failover chain replaces the main model: the first healthy entry serves,
a dead provider hands over loudly to the next, the winner sticks for
the session (RAM-only, never persisted), and cooled-down entries
re-enter rotation:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
  - provider_type: anthropic
    provider_config:
      model: claude-sonnet-4-6
      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

`apiKeyEnv` names the ENV indirection — a key VALUE never lives in the
yaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;
edits persist to the winning scope's file and go live from the next
turn. App Settings carries the same editor (env scope is read-only
there).

## Memory

<!-- parity: /memory -->

The long-term memory location. `memory:` may live in the user file or the
project file — project wins.

```yaml
memory:
  projectPath: ./memory        # inside the repo; committed with it
  userPath: ~/memory           # or a user-level store
```

CLI equivalent: `/memory` shows stats, `/memory maintain` runs consolidation —
neither edits paths; the section is the only way to set them. The live memory
controller re-reads the section (project resolution via `loadProjectMemoryConfig`),
so a path change applies without restart.

## Tool availability

<!-- parity: /tools -->

`tools:` maps a tool id (or `mcp:<server>`) to on/off. Scopes, deepest wins
per key; the host's hard capability floor can never be overridden on:

1. global — `~/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
2. project — `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
3. session — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` next to the session file
4. runtime — `--tools` flag / `FA_TOOLS` env (this run only)

```yaml
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: true                   # nested mcp: == mcp:<server> keys
```

CLI equivalent: `/tools enable|disable <id> [global|project|session]` writes
the matching scope file; `/tools` lists every id with its deciding scope;
`/tools reload` re-reads all scopes live. Disabled tools are hidden from the
model and tombstoned at execution. Edits apply live after a reload.

## Cubes

<!-- parity: /cube -->

Sandbox profile selection. `cube:` may live in the user or project file
(project wins). Manifests live in `<project>/.fah/cubes/<name>.yaml`.

```yaml
cube:
  enabled: true
  config: .fah/cubes/strict.yaml   # path to the cube manifest
```

CLI equivalent: `/cube use <name|path>` switches, `/cube off` disables,
`/cube list` lists manifests, `/cube reload` re-reads. Applies live via
`/cube`; a YAML edit applies at next boot (explicit `--cube`/`--cube-config`
flags beat both files).

<!-- parity: /mcp -->

Strict section — unknown shapes throw `ConfigException`. User file only.

```yaml
mcp:
  toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
  servers:
    fs:                        # stdio server
      command: npx
      args: [-y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-fs", /tmp]
      env: {KEY: value}

```

CLI equivalent: `/mcp` prints per-server status, `/mcp reload` re-reads the

connects lazily in the background.

## Redaction

<!-- parity: /redact -->

User file `redact:` section (issue #24 layered pipeline):

```yaml
redact:
  enabled: true
  blockMode: false             # deny credential-file reads outright
  layers:                      # per-layer toggles (priority order in docs/redaction.md)
    pii: true
  allowlist:                   # regex patterns that survive redaction (git SHAs, UUIDs)
    - "[0-9a-f]{40}"
  toolAllow: [bash]            # when non-empty, only these tools are redacted
  toolDeny: [web_fetch]        # never redacted; wins over toolAllow
```

CLI equivalent: `/redact on|off`, `/redact block on|off`, `/redact stats`,
`/redact layers`. The command toggles the live pipeline; the section is the
durable form written back when the CLI persists config. Redaction is
live-mutable — no restart needed either way.

## Compaction

Context-hiding engine choice (issue #148). User or project file (project
wins):

```yaml
compaction:
  engine: structured           # structured (default) | classic (rollback)
```

`structured` (the default since issue #287) hides records in place behind
one-line addressable markers (`compact_expand` restores any id or range
under a per-turn token budget); `classic` keeps the lossy summary
compaction — the legacy 1.0 rollback, selected through Settings →
Compaction (the app) or an explicit yaml/flag choice. Runtime override:
`fa --compaction-engine classic`; resolution is
flag > project > global > the structured default. Applies at
the next compaction.

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Prompts, TTSR & A2A

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
a2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints
  servers:
    peer:
      url: https://peer.example:8080
      token: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value]}      # env-resolved at boot — never a literal secret
fabric:                         # host discovery announcements (read-only:
  capabilities:                 # written by hosts, never user-edited)
    - name: yoclip.render
      description: Render the open project to MP4
```

`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they
configure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\${ENV}` reference
resolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an
unset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.

## Settings hub

<!-- parity: /settings -->

`/settings` is an interactive hub over the surfaces above (provider, model,
approval, cube, keys, MCP, DAP hub). It has no single config equivalent —
each arm edits the section documented for it. DAP hub settings are the one
surface NOT in config.yaml: the hub flow writes `~/.dap/config.json`
(identity keys, channels). Configure DAP through the hub flow or see
docs/dap.md; never hand-edit the DAP files while a hub client is running.

## Example invocations

- `point project memory at ./memory` → Memory section: `config` op `set`,
  key `memory.projectPath`, value `./memory` (project file is the default
  scope — created minimal if missing), then `check`, then report live
  application.
- `switch us to provider X` → Provider & keys: `config` op `set` for
  `provider:` (and `baseUrl:`) in the user file — global scope is the
  default for these keys; report next-boot application and the `/provider`
  equivalent.

- `add custom provider Y and switch to it` → Provider & keys: `config` op
  `get customProviders`, `config` op `set customProviders <extended JSON
  list>` (see the config-tool section), then `set provider openai-completions`,
  `set model <entry modelId>`, `set baseUrl <entry baseUrl>`; verify with
  `check`, report next-boot application and the `/provider` equivalent.
- `disable web_search for this project` → Tool availability: `config` op
  `set`, key `tools.web_search`, value `false` (project scope by default);
  report live after `/tools reload` semantics (host REPL) or next re-read.
- `configure cube backend Z` → Cubes: `config` op `set` for the `cube:`
  keys (project file for a repo default) and reference the manifest in
  `.fah/cubes/`.

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for
the run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI's, so ssh
sessions show the model's reasoning as it happens. The default `false`
keeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic
`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits
silent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use
(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless
`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no
flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml
output:
  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

Applies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file
reads, fast boot):

```yaml
projectContext:
  maxBytes: 32768 # merged budget; 0 = section off, no file reads
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for
product/store links — the App Store banner in the web/macOS apps, the
CLI, and the fa1.dev site generator all resolve the same values, so a
link changes in ONE place. Defaults are baked in; only overrides are
written. Strict parse: a non-map section, a non-URL value, or a
non-boolean banner is a `ConfigException`; unknown keys become notes,
never failures:

```yaml
links:
  appstore: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163
  testflight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK
  site: https://fa1.dev
  banner: true # false = no in-app App Store banner anywhere
```

`play:` (the Google Play release) stays ABSENT until the Android release
is live — every surface renders the Android slot as "coming soon" while
it is unset.

`banner: false` is the regression switch: the Get surface stays
byte-identical to the legacy UI. The section is user-file only (like
`tui:`/`fabric:`) and applies at next boot for the in-app banner; the
site renders the committed defaults (regen:
`dart run scripts/regen_site_store_block.dart`).

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

# Rework/verification run logs (transient artifacts — never committed).
# gh-2185: logs never belong in git at all — the whole dir is local-only
# (the tracked logs/app.log was purged from the index in the same change).

/network_mode.json

# memory store consolidated into .fah/memory (local-only, covered by the
# .fah/* rules above); the root copy is ignored so the old path can never
# re-track notes.
/input/
/outputs/
/memory/

content.text:
Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(committed, `memory/note/` — the user's files: read freely, write only via
`memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
====
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
====
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

    assert old in s, p
    open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new, 1))
    print("updated", p)
EOF

content.text:
flutter-app-goldens:
    name: Golden suite (macOS baselines)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # EXACT patch — the golden baselines are pixel-sensitive to the
      # engine's text stack; nightly renders them on the same 3.47.4.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.50.0'
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      - name: flutter test/goldens (issue #1856 pinned-font env)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        # TZ=UTC: the golden clock contract (golden_test_helper.dart) —
        # activity/session rows render fixed instants in the OS-local
        # zone; baselines embed UTC renderings, the runner's zone must
        # match or the helper fails loudly.
        env:
          TZ: UTC
        run: flutter test test/goldens
      # flutter_test writes the expected/actual/diff triple for every
      # failed comparison into goldens/failures/ — upload them so a
      # hosted-vs-capture drift can be EYEBALLED from the artifacts
      # instead of triangulated from percentages (the 2026-11-10
      # activity-golden red that passed locally).
      - name: Upload golden failure diffs
        if: failure()

#!/bin/bash
# Builds the Fa promo audio: voiceover segments (macOS say), a mixed 19 s VO
# track per language, and an ffmpeg-composed synth music bed.
#
# Upgrade path (see CREATIVE.md "TTS route"): replace the `say` calls with a
# hosted TTS (OpenAI tts-1-hd / ElevenLabs) writing the SAME segment files,
# then re-run this script — offsets and mixing stay identical.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

VO=assets/voiceover
AU=assets/audio
mkdir -p "$VO" "$AU" build/audio

DUR=19.0

# segment: <lang> <idx> <start_seconds> <text>
segments=(
  "en 1 0.40 A dashboard that is truly yours."
  "en 2 3.00 Your own apps, built by chat."
  "en 3 6.20 Fa lives inside every app you create."
  "en 4 9.40 It draws, speaks and plays."
  "en 5 12.50 Any provider — your keys never leave the Keychain."
  "en 6 15.70 Fa — AI Agent."
  "ru 1 0.40 Дашборд, который по-настоящему ваш."
  "ru 2 3.00 Свои приложения — созданные в чате."
  "ru 3 6.20 Fa живёт внутри каждого приложения."
  "ru 4 9.40 Он рисует, говорит и играет."
  "ru 5 12.50 Любой провайдер — ключи остаются в Keychain."
  "ru 6 15.70 Fa — ваш AI-агент."
)

voice_for() { [ "$1" = en ] && echo Samantha || echo Milena; }

for line in "${segments[@]}"; do
  lang=$(cut -d' ' -f1 <<<"$line"); idx=$(cut -d' ' -f2 <<<"$line")
  text=$(cut -d' ' -f4- <<<"$line")
  out="$VO/${lang}_0${idx}.m4a"
  if [ ! -s "$out" ]; then
    say -v "$(voice_for "$lang")" -r 172 -o "$out" "$text"
  fi
done

# --- mix VO segments onto a 19 s timeline per language -----------------------
for lang in en ru; do
  inputs=(); chain=""; labels=""
  i=0
  for line in "${segments[@]}"; do
    l=$(cut -d' ' -f1 <<<"$line"); [ "$l" = "$lang" ] || continue
    idx=$(cut -d' ' -f2 <<<"$line"); start=$(cut -d' ' -f3 <<<"$line")
    ms=$(python3 -c "print(int(float('$start')*1000))")
    f="build/audio/${lang}_${idx}.wav"
    ffmpeg -y -v error -i "$VO/${lang}_0${idx}.m4a" -ar 48000 -ac 1 \

    inputs+=(-i "$f")

# Project layout Reference for the `lib/`, `packages/`, `bin/`, `prompts/` subsystems. The Flutter app and its JS apps platform live in their own docs: > gh-2181: the full per-subsystem reference (moved verbatim from AGENTS.md) > is [sdk-subsystems.md](sdk-subsystems.md) + > [flutter-app-subsystems.md](flutter-app-subsystems.md); this file stays > the condensed map. - [flutter-app.md](flutter-app.md) — chat example, services, widgets - [js-apps.md](js-apps.md) — JS apps platform, demo apps, runtime pinning - [services.md](services.md) — Flutter app services one-liner - [system-integrations.md](system-integrations.md) — HomeKit, Calendar, CodeMie SSO - [cli.md](cli.md) — `fah`/`fa` CLI machinery, `/settings` hub, provider catalog - [providers.md](providers.md) — provider auth flows (chatgpt / codemie / dial / openrouter) - [fa-ui.md](fa-ui.md) — `packages/fa_ui/` reusable Flutter package ## Top-level tree ```mermaid graph TD R[flutter_agent/] R --> Lib[lib/ — pure Dart core
flutter_agent_harness] R --> T[test/ — mirrors lib/] R --> P[prompts/ — LLM prompts as Markdown] R --> Bin[bin/ — fah/fa CLI + serve_a2a + self_manage] R --> Pkg[packages/
fa_ui, fa_llm] R --> App[flutter_app/ — Flutter chat example] R --> Docs[docs/] R --> Site[site/ — GitHub Pages] R --> Scr[scripts/] R --> V[vendor/ — flutter_js, wasm_run, xterm] R --> Yo[yoclip/ — standalone video workspace] R --> Misc[coverage, profile-reports, store_artefacts,
generated, .fah, .repro, build] ``` - `lib/` is **pure Dart** (compiles for web; no `dart:io` — only `bin/` and `lib/io.dart` are IO entry points). `lib/src/` subsystems: ## Core tools / sinks - `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers `read`/`write`/`exec`, session modes `always-ask`/`write`/`yolo`, per-tool overrides, critical-pattern `bash` interceptor. `attachApproval` runs first in `beforeToolCall`; UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy = deny). - `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result). - `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: agent asks the user for a missing credential via injectable `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text). Grant returns `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted`); decline is a plain result. - `lib/src/tools/generate_image.dart` — `generate_image` tool: pure-Dart image generation saving PNG into sandbox `generated/`. Two dialects: OpenAI-compatible `POST {base}/images/generations` (default) and MiniMax `POST {base}/image_generation` (detected by `minimax` baseUrl). Bytes never enter chat context — only path + base64-staged `ImageContent`. Web-safe. - `lib/src/tools/inspect_image.dart` — `inspect_image` tool: dedicated vision-capable model analyzes a local image and returns text. Image payload never enters chat context. - `lib/src/tools/transcribe_audio.dart` — `transcribe_audio` tool: Whisper-compatible `/audio/transcriptions` (OpenAI / Groq / OpenRouter / local whisper.cpp). Pure-Dart `package:http` multipart. 25 MB cap. Audio never enters chat context. - `lib/src/tools/tool_format.dart` — tool result formatting helpers shared by media/shell tools. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant H as Host participant K as SessionKeysStore participant R as SecretRedactor H->>U: secretRequestHandler sheet alt grant (name + value + persisted) H->>K: save H->>R: register (next run: prompt list, bash $NAME, redaction) else cancel H-->>A: plain result end ``` - `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`: `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting `FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL` (resolved live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash. Wired around `builtinTools` in `AgentCli` + `AgentService`. `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment` (never replaces). - `lib/src/session_deadline.dart` — `SessionDeadline` (gh-1556): the ONE wall-clock budget source for a run — the temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412). Hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms; resolved live per turn through the session-correlation seam above, so a mid-session `/timer` change reaches the next bash exec and the next LLM request); `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline ` (headless AND interactive) and the TUI `/timer` slash-command write the same single session value (env < flag < `/timer`; later wins). While armed, every LLM request context carries a per-turn `time-left: …` line and one-shot `` steerings fire at the ladder crossings (~50%, the T-3min wrap-up/background-job-drain steer, T-30s); the TUI status line renders a countdown chip as a pure projection. Missing/invalid env = feature off, byte-for-byte today's behavior; an explicit invalid user spec is a clear `FormatException`, never a silent wrong clock. Pure Dart — the clock is injected, no `dart:io` in `lib/`. - `lib/src/env/memory_execution_env.dart` — `MemoryExecutionEnv`: pure-Dart in-memory `ExecutionEnv` (POSIX `/`-paths, default `Shell = UnavailableShell` reporting `shellUnavailable`). Default for tests and web consumers; shell-backed variants use `LocalShell` instead. - `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools for context hygiene. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`. - `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` + `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree navigation). Summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch. - `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — **single source of truth** for post-run compaction. **never re-implement auto-compaction in the host**; add hooks to `AutoCompactorHooks`. ```mermaid flowchart TD Start[run complete] --> Pass[compaction pass] Pass --> Fits{transcript fits?} Fits -- yes --> Done[done] Fits -- no --> Roles{roles point at
different models?} Roles -- yes --> Smol[try smol role] Smol --> Pass Roles -- no --> Main[try main role] Main --> Pass Pass -.transient error
5xx, connection closed/reset/aborted,
socket exception, stream closed.-> Wait[1s, then 2s backoff] Wait --> Pass Pass -. pass > 8 .-> Exhausted[give up] ``` ## Patch / read - `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing `HashlinePatcher`. Stale tags reject before any write. `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag. - `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors: `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be combined with a selector. - `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap. - `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`, `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`) via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`; without it a clean "not supported" note. ## Protocol tooling - `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename): pure-Dart JSON-RPC over `LspTransport`; `.dart` → `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`; projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`. Lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff. Renames apply all-or-nothing through the env. IO via `lib/io.dart` + `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`. 1-indexed line/character; missing server = clean note, never a crash. - `lib/src/mcp/` — MCP servers from `mcp:` section of `~/.fah/config.yaml` (strict `ConfigException` parsing). Stdio (`command`/`args`/`env`, NDJSON — **NOT** LSP's Content-Length) and remote (`url`, streamable-http default or legacy sse, `headers`). Message-level `McpTransport`; stdio framing pure Dart over `McpByteChannel` (process via `lib/io.dart`), HTTP transports pure Dart over injectable `package:http` (web gets remote; stdio = "not supported"). `McpManager` connects lazily in background, per-server `connecting`/`connected`/`failed` status, reconnect with capped backoff. Tools register as `mcp____` (exec tier, description prefixed with origin, inputSchema verbatim). Results map MCP blocks onto ours; `isError` throws; timeouts `mcp.toolCallTimeoutMs`. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Connecting: lazy, background Connecting --> Connected: handshake ok Connecting --> Failed: handshake fail Connected --> Connected: tool call Failed --> Reconnecting: backoff timer Reconnecting --> Connecting: retry Failed --> Failed: budget exhausted Connected --> Idle: 5 min idle note right of Failed: per-server status surfaced via onChanged ``` ## Providers / models See [providers.md](providers.md) for the full provider catalog. - `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles `default`/`smol`/`slow`/`plan` with fallback chains, key rotation (`ApiKeyRing` over `NAME`/`NAME_2`/…), 429 mid-turn take-over (`FallbackStreamFunction`, **never silent**). Watchdogs (`provider_common.dart`): `providerConnectTimeout` 60s, `providerStreamIdleTimeout` 120s between bytes — wedged endpoint errors out so the resolver can fail over. Config: `roles:`/`modelOverrides:`/`retry:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` (invalid schema = `ConfigException`). Shared models: `media_model_slots.dart` (shared with app's `MediaModelsStore`) and `models_config.dart` (per-slot media overrides + named custom model definitions `/model ` resolves; persisted by host). - `lib/src/ttsr/` — time-traveling stream rules: regex matched against streaming deltas; on match abort, inject rule bodies as hidden `` message, retry after 50ms. Persisted via `TtsrSessionSink`. Guards: once-per-session, `maxInjectionsPerTurn`. Config: `ttsr:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` + project `.fah/rules.yaml`. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Provider participant T as TTSR matcher participant Run as Agent run Provider->>T: streaming delta alt regex matches T-->>Run: abort current stream Run->>Run: inject rule body as
hidden Run->>Provider: retry (50ms) else no match Provider-->>Run: append delta end Note over T: TtsrSessionSink guards:
once-per-session, maxInjectionsPerTurn ``` ## Skills / context - `lib/src/skills/skills.dart` — agent skills: `//SKILL.md`, roots project (`.fah/skills`, `.agents/skills`) > user (`~/.fah/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`), first-name-wins. Only metadata enters the system prompt; bodies loaded via `read`. - `lib/src/prompts/project_context.dart` — `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` auto-merged into the system prompt: cwd → git root, farthest-first, `` annotations, 32 KiB leaf-first budget; optional `~/.fah/AGENTS.md` first. CLI: `/skill: [args]`, `/skills`. ## Subagents / messaging - `lib/src/task/` — `task` tool: parallel subagents, batch `{context, tasks[]}` + `background`; children never get `task` (no nesting); `explore`→`smol`, `review`→`slow`; `outputSchema` ONE fix retry; child failure = per-item error. `/tasks` lists jobs, `/tasks cancel `; completions re-enter parent as async-result (`agent://`). Subagents retained: real JSONL child sessions, `task_status`/`task_observe`/`task_send`, child-only `reply` + sibling `agent_message` (pending-queue + hop-capped), `completed_without_reply` notice. - `lib/src/messaging/` — messaging fabric: every agent owns a file inbox behind the `MessagingRepository` interface (`send`/`peek`/`drain`/`directory`). `FileMessagingRepository` over `ExecutionEnv`: `//inbox|read/.json`, timestamp-ordered, sanitized dirs, torn writes skipped. `mailboxPrefix` namespaces mailboxes — ids with `/` are absolute cross-instance addresses (`/main`). `agent_message` targets siblings/main/absolute; `agent_directory` lists with pending counts (`.id` markers keep real ids). UI: `/agents` rows show `mail:N` (no ✉ in CLI font), app's `AgentsSection` shows `✉N`. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Sender participant FS as //inbox participant W as Watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) participant Run as Agent run S->>FS: write .json W->>FS: poll FS-->>W: new file W->>Run: start turn (idle wake) Run->>Run: drain via Agent.externalSteeringSource
(persists in session, reads like chat) Note over W: 10-run streak cap w/o user input
breaks ping-pong loops ``` - `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory: `MemoryController` over `flutter_agent_memory` (hosted pub.dev), `execution_env_kb_storage` (KbStorage → ExecutionEnv), `memory_add`/`memory_search`/`memory_list` tools (`memoryTools(controller, onChanged:)`), and `` prompt section (`formatPromptSection()` BOTH scopes; entities via `KBFileParser` — raw file's first line is the `---` delimiter) cached by host, recomposed after startup + on every `memory_add` (CLI `_refreshMemorySection`, app `AgentService`). Phase 2: `compaction_memory_hook` (smol role, non-blocking), `maintain()` (levels + consolidate, 24h stamp), triggers on session start + `/memory maintain`. - `lib/src/a2a/` — A2A (Agent2Agent) interop: `a2a_client.dart` (Agent Card + JSON-RPC + SSE), `a2a_config.dart` (`a2a:` yaml section, `${NAME}` env tokens), `a2a_manager.dart` (lazy per-server connect, A2A task state → subagent lifecycle), `a2a_server.dart` (request handler). `task` agent type `a2a:` runs remote agents as subagents; `/a2a` shows server status; `fa serve --a2a [--port N] [--token T]` mounts as endpoint (`bin/serve_a2a.dart`). ## CLI See [cli.md](cli.md) for full CLI machinery and the `/settings` hub. ## `packages/fa_ui/` See [fa-ui.md](fa-ui.md) for the full reusable widget package. ## `flutter_app/` See [flutter-app.md](flutter-app.md) for the chat example structure, shim re-exports, and widgets. ## Other - `docs/subagents/` — the subagents-2.0 + long-term-memory master plan (phased: memory package publish, memory foundation, memory-aware compaction, session-backed retained subagents, agent-type menu); update the checklists there as work lands. - `site/` — static GitHub Pages landing; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds the web demo into `app/` (never committed). `site/privacy.html` is the published privacy policy (`PRIVACY.md` in the repo root is the source text — keep both in sync; the onboarding privacy page links to `https://fa1.dev/privacy.html`). - `scripts/` — codegen and quality-gate scripts.

# vendor/ — patched dependency forks (KEEP)

`vendor/` holds **deliberate patched forks** of upstream packages. This note
is the written rationale the gh-2185 root-hygiene pass requires, so future
hygiene sweeps keep the directory instead of "cleaning" it away.

| Fork | Why it exists |
| --- | --- |
| `vendor/dart_tui` | keyboard-protocol fixes pending/absent upstream |
| `vendor/flutter_inappwebview_*` (linux/macos/windows stubs) | platform stubs so desktop builds compile without the heavy plugin on hosts that don't need it |
| `vendor/quickjs_runtime` | JS-apps runtime pin |
| `vendor/wasm_run` + `vendor/wasm_run_flutter` | wasm runtime fork (the iOS framework download path upstream is gone — the jniLibs are committed, see `.gitignore`) |
| `vendor/xterm` | terminal widget pin |

The tracked `pubspec_overrides.yaml` (237 B) points `dart_tui` at
`vendor/dart_tui`. Local + CI builds use the fork; the published
`flutter_agent_harness` package keeps the hosted dependency — **this file
never ships to pub.dev** (it is excluded from the publish payload). Do not
delete it as "leftover config": local and CI builds resolve `dart_tui`
through it.

`pub.dev` ships the hosted packages; the forks ride the repo checkout only
(`stage_publish_package.sh` prunes `/vendor` from the staged payload).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gh-2185 AC7 — repo-root allow-list guard.

The repository root carries ONLY first-class project artifacts (source,
docs, configs, CI). gh-2185 purged the runtime-state JSONs, the tracked
log, the 920-file root memory store and the duplicate-store dirs; this
guard keeps the root that way:

  1. TRACKED LENS — every depth-0 entry of `git ls-files` must be
     allow-listed. A stray new root file fails the gate (pre-commit via
     ci_fast_gate.sh stage_analyze; whole-tree in the CI `static` job).
  2. TEMPLATE CLASS (gh-2185 AC6) — any filesystem entry at the root
     whose name embeds an unexpanded `${...}` fails outright, tracked or
     not: that is the artifact class of the empty
     `${Directory.systemTemp.path}` directory the audit found (a Dart
     string template executed verbatim as a path). No shipped writer
     produces such names — grep evidence in the gh-2185 PR — so the only
     way one appears is the same quoting bug class again.

Allow-list additions are NOT mechanical: they need a card-visibility
review (add the entry here AND to the inventory table in the ticket/PR).

Usage:
  python3 scripts/check_root_allowlist.py [--repo <path>] [--self-test]
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

# Depth-0 entries allowed to be tracked at the repo root (gh-2185 KEEP
# table minus the purged rows: runtime-state JSONs, logs/, memory/,
# goal/, knowledgebase/, tools/ are NOT here on purpose).
ALLOWED = frozenset({
    # tracked root configs/docs (the KEEP rows)
    ".crap-baseline.json",
    ".gitattributes",
    ".gitignore",
    ".pubignore",
    "AGENTS.md",
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md",  # release tooling reads it at the root (gh-1452)
    "GOAL.md",
    "LICENSE",
    "PRIVACY.md",
    "README.md",
    "SECURITY.md",
    "analysis_options.yaml",
    "crap4dart.yaml",
    "crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml",
    "dart_test.yaml",
    "install_local.sh",
    "pubspec.yaml",
    "pubspec_overrides.yaml",  # the vendor-fork switch — deliberate, docs/vendor.md
    # source / content dirs
    "bench",
    "bin",
    "blog",
    "browser_ext",
    "docs",
    "example",
    "flutter_app",
    "js-ext-registry",
    "lib",
    "office_addin",
    "packages",
    "prompts",
    "schema",
    "scripts",
    "sdk",  # sdk/web — the wire-protocol reference client (conformance-gated)
    "site",
    "store_artefacts",  # store-metadata changelogs (docs/agents/commits-releases.md)
    "test",
    "tool",  # ONE tool dir (gh-2185 AC9)
    "vendor",  # patched forks — rationale: docs/vendor.md
    "yoclip",  # fa promo-video workspace (binaries purged per-class)
    # curated agent-tooling state
    ".fah",
    ".github",
    ".kimi-code",
    ".dmtools",
    ".pr-assets",
})

STATE_DIR_HINT = (
    "runtime state belongs in .fah/state/ (app stores, via "
    "flutter_app/lib/services/app_state_paths.dart) or .fah/memory/ "
    "(project memory); logs/dumps are gitignored (logs/, test-results/, "
    "profile-reports/, generated/). See docs/agents/project-layout.md "
    "(repo-root hygiene contract). Allow-list additions need a "
    "card-visibility review — edit scripts/check_root_allowlist.py "
    "deliberately, never to silence the gate."
)

TEMPLATE_HINT = (
    "an entry whose NAME embeds an unexpanded ${...} template — the "
    "gh-2185 artifact class (a Dart string template executed verbatim as "
    "a path). Delete it and fix the writer that quoted the expression."
)


def tracked_root_entries(repo: str) -> set:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files"], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout
    return {line.split("/", 1)[0] for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()}


def template_named_entries(repo: str) -> list:
    return [e for e in sorted(os.listdir(repo)) if "${" in e]


def check(repo: str) -> int:
    failures = []

    stray = sorted(tracked_root_entries(repo) - ALLOWED)
    if stray:
        failures.append(
            "tracked root entries outside the allow-list:\n"
            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in stray)
            + f"\n{STATE_DIR_HINT}"
        )

    tmpl = template_named_entries(repo)
    if tmpl:
        failures.append(
            "template-named root entries (unexpanded ${...}):\n"
            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in tmpl)
            + f"\n{TEMPLATE_HINT}"
        )

    if failures:
        print("root allow-list guard: FAILED\n")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        return 1
    print(f"root allow-list guard: ok ({len(ALLOWED)} allow-listed entries)")
    return 0


def self_test() -> int:
    """Fixture repo: clean passes; a stray file and the ${...} template
    class both fail."""
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="root-allowlist-selftest-")
    try:
        repo = os.path.join(tmp, "repo")
        os.makedirs(repo)
        git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(  # noqa: E731
            ["git", *a], cwd=repo,
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
        )
        git("init", "-q")
        for name, content in (("README.md", "# t\n"), ("pubspec.yaml", "name: t\n")):
            with open(os.path.join(repo, name), "w") as fh:
                fh.write(content)
        git("add", "-A")
        git("-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-qm", "init")
        here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
        guard = os.path.join(here, "check_root_allowlist.py")

        def run(*args):
            return subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, guard, *args], cwd=repo,
                capture_output=True, text=True,
            )

        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print(f"self-test: clean fixture FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        with open(os.path.join(repo, "chat_read_cursors.json"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("{}\n")
        git("add", "-A")
        git("-c", "user.email=t@t", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-qm", "stray")
        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 1 or "chat_read_cursors.json" not in r.stdout:
            print(f"self-test: stray-file case FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, "${Directory.systemTemp.path}"))
        r = run()
        if r.returncode != 1 or "systemTemp" not in r.stdout:
            print(f"self-test: template-entry case FAILED\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
            return 1

        print("self-test: PASS (clean ok, stray fails, template class fails)")
        return 0
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)

stage_analyze() {
  # gh-2181: the AGENTS.md size ceiling runs in THIS stage — AGENTS.md
  # edits classify as docs (docs/*.md → analyze is the docs scope's only
  # stage), so a docs-only commit that regrows the entry file must fail
  # here. Same script the ci.yml static job runs (wiring pinned by
  # test/agents_md_size_guard_test.dart).
  bash scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders
    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
====
      # gh-2181: AGENTS.md is the agent ENTRY document (harness budget
      # ~19 KB — a larger file silently disables its own tail). Ceiling
      # <= 300 lines / <= 20480 bytes; the pre-commit path runs the same
      # script via ci_fast_gate.sh stage_analyze. Wiring pinned by
      # test/agents_md_size_guard_test.dart.
      - name: AGENTS.md size ceiling guard (gh-2181)

local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
====
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          # Issue #1696: capture the raw exit code so the classification
          # step below can tell the runner-process SIGABRT class (134)
          # apart from ordinary test failures.
          set +e
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
          code=$?
          set -e
          echo "$code" > test-results/exit-code
          exit "$code"
      # Issue #1696: the runner process itself can abort natively (glibc
      # heap detector, exit 134) with a fully green report — the leg goes
      # red without any test failure. Annotate that class in the step
      # summary so a recurrence self-identifies; the leg stays red and the
      # file-bot behavior is unchanged.
      - name: classify native abort (issue #1696)
        if: failure()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/classify_native_abort.py
          test-results/exit-code
          test-results/integration.json >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
